subject: music
intro: Music leads into the performing and recording professions: playing and singing for audiences, directing and composing, shaping sound in the studio, and teaching the discipline at university level.

roles.title: Musicians and Singers
roles.what: Play one or more musical instruments or sing, performing on stage, for broadcasting, or for sound or video recording — rehearsing and keeping technique sharp between engagements.
roles.where: The elements of music — melody, scales and modes, rhythm and metre, tonality — and the seven areas of study from Baroque concerto to Hindustani classical give performers the analytical ear behind interpretation.

roles.title: Music Directors and Composers
roles.what: Conduct, direct, plan and lead instrumental or vocal performances by musical artists or groups such as orchestras, bands, choirs and glee clubs, or create original works of music.
roles.where: The structure topics — sonata form, theme and variations, verse and chorus — train the architectural hearing composers need; music for stage and screen covers scoring to picture; notation units cover the written craft.

roles.title: Sound Engineering Technicians
roles.what: Assemble and operate equipment to record, synchronise, mix, edit or reproduce sound, including music, voices or sound effects, for theater, video, film, television, podcasts and other productions.
roles.where: The music technology and production topics — sampling, looping, reverb, delay, overdubbing, multi-tracking, drum machines — and the EDM area of study's breakdown, build up and drop are studio practice by another name.

roles.title: Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in drama, music and the arts, including applied music performance and academic music study — combining teaching with their own research and creative practice.
roles.where: The listening syllabus's musical elements and seven areas of study, plus the music-cognition extension on why brains find some patterns irresistible, are the lecture and seminar stock of a university music post.

roles.title: Disc Jockeys, Except Radio
roles.what: Play prerecorded music for live audiences at venues or events such as clubs, parties or wedding receptions, using techniques such as mixing, cutting or sampling to manipulate recordings.
roles.where: The music-for-dance area of study — tango, salsa, EDM — trains the beat and genre fluency DJing needs, while the technology unit's loops, sampling and production techniques are the craft's raw material.
